question: Both A and B sells their watch at the rate of Rs. 5000 per watch. A earned a profit of 25 percent while B incurred a loss of 10 percent. What is the ratio of cost prices of A and B?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of A = Rs. 5000

Selling price of B = Rs. 5000

Profit of A = 25%

Loss of B = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 + Profit%)

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 - Loss%)

Ratio = CP of A / CP of B

**Calculation:**

CP of A = 5000 / (1 + 25/100)

⇒ CP of A = 5000 / 1.25

⇒ CP of A = 4000

CP of B = 5000 / (1 - 10/100)

⇒ CP of B = 5000 / 0.9

⇒ CP of B = 5555.56

Ratio of CP of A to CP of B = 4000 / 5555.56

⇒ Ratio = 0.72

⇒ Ratio = 18 : 25

**The ratio of cost prices of A and B is 18 ∶ 25.**
